overview.description: This section fills any gaps in DNA theory before you start manipulating it. If you're confident, skim and move on - but a solid mental model of base pairing, polarity and charge underpins every downstream technique.
objectives: describe DNA structure and antiparallel base pairing
explain why DNA carries a uniform negative charge
use a sequence viewer (Benchling/SnapGene) to read a .dna map

steps.description: This section fills any gaps in DNA theory before you start manipulating it. If you're confident, skim and move on - but a solid mental model of base pairing, polarity and charge underpins every downstream technique.
steps.intro: This section fills any gaps in DNA theory before you start manipulating it. If you're confident, skim and move on - but a solid mental model of base pairing, polarity and charge underpins every downstream technique.

instructions.title: Review structure
instructions.description: Refresh the double helix, 5'->3' polarity, A-T/G-C pairing and the phosphate backbone's negative charge.

instructions.title: Open a real plasmid
instructions.description: Download a plasmid (e.g. pET-15b) from Addgene and open it in your viewer to see features, ORIs and restriction sites.

instructions.title: Connect theory to charge
instructions.description: Note that each base adds one negative charge - the basis for gel electrophoresis later.

submission.description: Annotate a plasmid map in your viewer, labelling the origin of replication, resistance gene, promoter and multiple cloning site.
